subject: Addendum: Operator access, key escrow, and cross-border controls for Private Deployment
messages:
From: Ella Rodriguez <ella.rodriguez@medipharm.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Baines <tbaines@medipharm.com>, Lisa Chen <l.chen@medipharm.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment - operator access / key escrow needs

Marcus,

Thanks for yesterday's demo — the VPC/on-prem option looks promising. Before we can proceed to procurement we need a short contractual addendum that: 1) defines operator (Redwood) break-glass access procedures for escalations, 2) confirms customer-controlled keys and the escrow process (if any), and 3) explains how backups/DR replicas are handled across borders (we operate primarily in US & EU).

Specific asks from Legal & InfoSec:
- Confirmation that customer controls KMS keys (HSM preferred) and that Redwood cannot decrypt customer data without a documented, auditable break-glass process.
- If Redwood requires emergency key escrow, we need the escrow to be a sealed HSM escrow with dual custody and explicit approvals from our security contact and Redwood legal.
- Full subprocessors snapshot (current) and commitment to 30-day notice before adding new subprocessors that have access to metadata or logs.
- Clarify whether DR replicas will ever be stored outside customer-chosen regions and the lawful basis for cross-border replication.

Can you loop in legal? We need a short addendum (1-2 pages) and a runbook for the break-glass flow.

Thanks,
Ella
Ella Rodriguez
VP, IT Security — MediPharm Solutions

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ella Rodriguez <ella.rodriguez@medipharm.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment - operator access / key escrow needs

Hi Ella — great to meet yesterday (thanks Tom).

High level answers up front:
- Customer-managed keys are supported. For Dedicated and Private we offer a customer-controlled KMS/HSM integration where your key material never leaves your control plane.
- We do support an optional, tightly-scoped emergency escrow: keys are sealed in a customer-managed HSM under dual custody; Redwood cannot access it without a two-party (customer security + Redwood legal) approval and an auditable workflow.
- DR/backup replication is configurable per deployment. By default we keep replicas in-region; cross-border replication only occurs with explicit customer consent and must be listed in the DPA addendum.
- Subprocessors: we'll attach the current snapshot; Redwood commits to 30-day notice for changes that could access logs or metadata.

Neha/Monica — can you take point on a short addendum + a 1-page runbook for the break-glass that includes: approval roles, SLA for approval response, logs retained, and an audit trail? I can share our subprocessors CSV and an initial redline.

Action items: Marcus to attach redline + subprocessors snapshot; Legal to prepare addendum draft; Ella to confirm any required data residency for DR.

Cheers,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachment: subprocessors_snapshot_2026-06-18.csv (stub)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ella Rodriguez <ella.rodriguez@medipharm.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment - operator access / key escrow needs

Ella — looping in Legal & Product Ops. A few clarifying points from Legal:

1) "Customer-controlled keys" — we propose contract language that explicitly states Redwood will not possess key material; integration is via customer-side HSM (KMIP or cloud KMS) and Redwood is cryptographically prevented from exfiltrating keys. If customer requires escrow we will accept a sealed, customer-owned HSM module that is physically and logically controlled by the customer (Redwood will never hold the sealed key).

2) "Emergency break-glass" — Legal requires: a documented escalation path, two independent approvals (customer security lead + Redwood legal counsel), and a manual override only in life-safety or critical-SLA breach scenarios. All actions must be logged and retained for five years. We will include a clause requiring joint post-incident review within 30 days.

3) "Subprocessors" — we will provide a CSV listing vendor name, function, country, and whether the vendor has access to logs/metrics. Redwood's default is to avoid giving subprocessors access to plaintext content for private deployments; any exception will be explicitly listed with purpose and retention.

4) "Cross-border backups" — product notes: backups are configurable; default is region-locked. Cross-border replication requires affirmative customer instruction and must be recorded in the deployment manifest; we'll include a clause that Redwood will not move replicas outside agreed boundaries unless legally compelled and we will notify the customer unless prohibited.

Karthik — please draft the operational runbook (1 page) describing the sequence: 1) Incident raised, 2) Customer security authorization, 3) Redwood legal approval, 4) Escrow HSM unseal, 5) Temporary access window & logging, 6) Re-sealing and post-incident report. Include retention windows and contact points.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Legal — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ella Rodriguez <ella.rodriguez@medipharm.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment - operator access / key escrow needs

Ella — attaching the suggested addendum (redline) and the operator runbook Karthik drafted. These are intentionally terse so legal can review quickly.

Attachments (stubs):
- RWD-7892_addendum_redline_20260618.pdf (2-page redline showing: customer KMS control language, escrow conditions, escrow dual-custody steps, subprocessors notice window, and data residency clause)
- operator_runbook_v1.md (one-page runbook with step-by-step approvals and log retention)
- subprocessors_snapshot_2026-06-18.csv (current vendors and their country / access level)

We can gate the DocuSign envelope to MediPharm's legal once you confirm the redline items below: 1) dual-custody condition for escrow OK? 2) 30-day subprocessors notice OK? 3) Cross-border replication only with written instruction OK?

If yes, I'll kick off DocuSign and share the link.

— Marcus
Attachment: RWD-7892_addendum_redline_20260618.pdf (stub), operator_runbook_v1.md (stub)

From: Ella Rodriguez <ella.rodriguez@medipharm.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Baines <tbaines@medipharm.com>, Lisa Chen <l.chen@medipharm.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment - operator access / key escrow needs

Marcus / Neha — thank you. Quick answers: 1) Dual-custody escrow HSM — acceptable. 2) 30-day subprocessors notice — acceptable, but we will require a clause that allows us to suspend onboarding of new subprocessors that touch metadata during a 15-day review window. 3) Cross-border replication — we require replicas for EU-stored data to remain within EU unless we approve in writing.

Also, one more question about backups: if the deployment is configured to replicate to a DR site in a different region, will Redwood maintain separate encryption keys per-region, or will they reuse the same key? We prefer separate keys per region with customer control.

If you can update the redline to capture the 15-day review suspension right and per-region key requirement, we can send this to legal for signature. Please enqueue the DocuSign after the redline is updated.

Thanks,
Ella

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ella Rodriguez <ella.rodriguez@medipharm.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment - operator access / key escrow needs

Ella — thanks for the quick review. We've accepted the two edits: 1) a 15-day suspension right on onboarding subprocessors that affect metadata; and 2) per-region, customer-managed keys for any configured DR/replica locations. I've updated the redline and queued the DocuSign envelope to MediPharm Legal. Link: https://www.docusign.com/rooms/abcd-efgh-20260619 (stub).

Next steps:
- Marcus to monitor DocuSign and confirm when signed.
- Karthik to export the final runbook and attach to deployment manifest.
- Neha to include the addendum as an amendment to the Master DPA.

Looking forward — I'll ping once it's fully executed.

Best,
Marcus
